assign.outcome:
**One renderer, one vocabulary, and a url seam that is genuinely finished — and the realm still fails my exit test, on the same defect it has failed on four times, one level deeper each time.**

**My exit condition, named before I walked.** An empty list needs three things: (1) exactly one class draws a configured page; (2) the words a control writes are the words the file stores are the words the url says are the words the reader reads, and every one of the seven can be **set, saved and sent** by the same reader; (3) no control writes a key nothing reads, and no renderer reads a key nothing writes — *in both directions, on every page, including the pages the realm makes*. **(1) is true now. (2) and (3) are not.**

**All six of my fourth-visit items landed.** A made page draws its own children (`make/page.js:72`, `:103`), the blocks reach the page (`build/draw.js:28`, one renderer two callers), the builder is three columns at 1280 with its live stage **619px down** (was 2,100), `BuildStage` is 98 lines that render a `PagingStage`, the stable/dynamic split is one flag, and taking a nest out is sendable.

**Renderers: two → one.** `stage.js:45 PagingStage` is the only class that draws a configured page, and all five callers go through it. What is left beside it is five *instruments* that draw from something other than the seven words — the swap visuals, the navigation lab, the full-screen rail app, the hub's four miniatures — each with a reason on its own page. And **one dead one**: `make/tabs.js:47 tabs_items()` is called by nothing in the repo.

**Vocabularies: one, and it holds harder than last time.** `blocks.js:215` now carries four fields per control — `axis` (the file), `block` (the rail), `label` (the reader), `key` (the address) — so the rail, the bar, the file and the url are the same six names *by construction*, not by discipline.

**The seam, measured.** Seven non-default words in one cold address open right; the old keys still open, so no saved link broke; all seven dropdowns write the reader's words; `?nest=` off round-trips. **100 loads at 1280 and 3440, zero page errors, zero sideways scroll.**

![A page you made, running inside another page — its tab strip reads Overview, Pricing, Docs, Contact, and its real children are Today and Later](shots/nested-made-page-1280.png)

**But look at the picture.** That is `Notes` — a page you made — running inside the blog preset by `?nest=/imagine/paging/make/notes/`. Opened on its own it reads **Today · Later** with two working links. Nested, it draws the demo's four canned tabs. `stage.js:283` has the whole node in hand and `stage.js:263` throws its children and its blocks away. **It is the exact defect the last pass fixed, one level in** — which is now four rounds of the same shape: the seven words, then the blocks, now the nest.

**And two of the seven words can be saved by no control at all.** Make writes four, Build writes three — five between them. **`room` and `type size` are set by no editor**, and the bar on a page you made is a *preview*: I set Room to Wide on `/make/notes/`, the address said `?room=wide`, the file stayed at `reading`, and a bare reload came back `reading`. The only thing that saves all seven is the drawer's *Make this a page*, and it only makes a **new** page. The one line that closes it in Build is already written down in [doc/builder.md](/imagine/paging/doc/builder/).

**The infinite-potential question, answered.** *It holds on the reading side and is closed on the keeping side.* A reader can generate 100,800 whole pages the authors never wrote — six navigations × eight contents × four rooms × seven arrangements × five content colours × five page colours × three type sizes — **every one of them addressable**: I opened `?content-colour=dark&page-colour=tint&type-size=display&navigation=rail&room=wide&arrangement=rail-right&content=dashboard` cold and got exactly that page. On top of that: any of those can hold **any page inside it** by url (a page *I* made ran inside a blog preset); [Cross](/imagine/paging/cross/) crosses any word with any other and draws 42 live pages at once; a built page's content is arbitrary markdown, its own children as cards, or any of eleven real template families; and the **Code** button prints the runnable `page.js` for any of it, which is a real door out of the vocabulary. That is genuinely open-ended. **The one thing still closed is that nothing you generate can be kept and then changed.** Save is one-way: a configuration becomes a page, and from that moment five of its seven words are editable and two are not, in a tool whose whole promise was *"configure it without having to write it out as a new page"*. The address is the only complete editor in the realm, and it writes to nothing.

**Seven items, ranked, in the `log` lines below** — one M and the rest S. Nothing cosmetic in the top three.
